Cork Lotto Jackpot Win

The National Lottery claims their September decision to reduce the ball pool from 47 to 45 improved jackpot odds from 1 in 10.7M to 1 in 8.1M, yielding its first €5.66M winner in Cork.

The mathematical change is verified: removing balls 46 and 47 directly improved combination probabilities by 24%, and an authentic €5,664,896 winning Quick Pick was sold at Mahon Point Shopping Centre.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.83, +0.87) — Greater Good

A PERSON IN Cork became the first player to win a jackpot since the National Lottery removed two balls from the draw, bagging more than €5 million.

The player won €5,664,896 in Wednesday night’s draw after buying a ticket in Eason’s bookshop in Mahon Point Shopping Centre.

The Quick Pick ticket was purchased on Tuesday 6 October.

Advertisement

The number of balls in the Lotto draw was reduced from 47 to 45 in September, with numbers 46 and 47 removed. This improved the odds of winning, going from one in 10.7 million to one in 8.1 million.

National Lottery spokesperson Darragh O’Dwyer said the win was 
“a landmark moment for our new Lotto game”.

“We are encouraging all Lotto players in Cork to carefully check their tickets today,” he said.

“If it is you, get in touch with our prize claims team as soon as possible, and in the meantime, keep that ticket somewhere safe.”

The winning ticket holder is advised to sign the back of their ticket and contact the National Lottery Prize Claims team on 1800 666 222 or email claims@lottery.ie.
